biography.plain_text: Bo Göransson was a Swedish entrepreneur who expanded Intrum Justitia from a family debt-collection business into an international credit-management group. He bought the company from his father and later sold down his substantial stake. Through Parkerhouse, he also invested in factoring businesses and became a major shareholder in the internet-services company Online Group.

long_biography.plain_text:
Credit-management entrepreneur Bo Göransson looked for opportunities in the paperwork companies struggled to manage. After an employee noticed piles of receivables at a television shop, Göransson and his team developed a service that handled these files for clients and shared the sums recovered. The business spread across Nordic markets.

His approach to expansion also involved partnerships. When a Swiss entrepreneur asked to use the Justitia name, Göransson proposed going into business together, creating the group's first venture outside Sweden. Later, he sought a common identity for businesses trading under different names and chose Intrum Justitia after finding inspiration in a crime novel.
